title: Battery needs charging
fullDescription:
One flash on Pride Go-Go / Victory / Jazzy control panel means battery is below operational threshold.

Charge fully (8-12 hours).

Safety note: deep discharge harms battery longevity.
whenToCallPro: For medical devices, contact manufacturer support or your healthcare provider before attempting service

faq.a: Modern chargers auto-stop; safe to leave overnight.

title: Battery connection issue
fullDescription:
Two flashes point to corroded or loose battery terminals, or internal battery failure.

Inspect, clean, tighten terminals.

Safety note: disconnect power before servicing; wear gloves.

fixSteps.title: Clean terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Remove corrosion with baking soda; retighten.

whenToCallPro: For medical devices, contact manufacturer support or your healthcare provider before attempting service

faq.a: Most Pride use SLA; some newer models lithium — check manual.

title: Left motor fault
fullDescription:
Three flashes indicate left motor circuit problem. Pride Jazzy power wheelchairs most commonly see this.

Check motor plug; professional service otherwise.

Safety note: stop using until resolved.
whenToCallPro: Contact Pride dealer for motor service

faq.a: Advanced DIY; some motors have user-serviceable brushes.

title: Right motor fault
fullDescription:
Four flashes indicate right motor circuit problem. Diagnosis mirrors left motor fault.

Check right motor plug; dealer service if needed.

Safety note: asymmetric drive is a safety hazard.
whenToCallPro: Contact Pride dealer for motor service

faq.a: Rare; more likely a controller fault.

title: Parking brake / freewheel
fullDescription:
Five flashes mean the scooter is in freewheel mode — brake released for pushing. Engage drive lever.

Move lever to drive position.

Safety note: never use freewheel on slopes.

fixSteps.title: Engage drive
fixSteps.instruction: Push freewheel lever to drive position.

whenToCallPro: For medical devices, contact manufacturer support or your healthcare provider before attempting service

title: Drive inhibited (charger connected)
fullDescription:
Six flashes indicate charger is still plugged in or inhibit input is active.

Unplug charger.

Safety note: safety feature — do not disable.
whenToCallPro: For medical devices, contact manufacturer support or your healthcare provider before attempting service

faq.a: Then inhibit input may be stuck — see dealer.

title: Throttle out of neutral
fullDescription:
Seven flashes indicate throttle was pressed at startup or throttle sensor fault.

Release throttle, power cycle.

Safety note: if persistent, have throttle inspected.
whenToCallPro: For medical devices, contact manufacturer support or your healthcare provider before attempting service

title: Controller fault
fullDescription:
Eight flashes indicate main controller (Penny+Giles, Dynamic, Curtis) fault.

Contact dealer.

Safety note: do not drive.

title: Comms fault between tiller and controller
fullDescription:
Nine flashes = tiller/joystick lost communication with controller. Check and reseat cables.

If persistent, cable or controller service.

Safety note: intermittent control = safety hazard.

title: Overvoltage condition
shortDescription: Battery or charger voltage too high.
fullDescription:
Ten flashes occur if battery voltage exceeds safe limits — often from using an incorrect charger or from regeneration on downhill.

Disconnect charger; verify correct model. Wait for voltage to normalize.

Safety note: using wrong charger can damage batteries.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect
fixSteps.instruction: Remove charger; verify specs match scooter.

whenToCallPro: For medical devices, contact manufacturer support or your healthcare provider before attempting service

faq.a: Check manual — usually 24V with matching amperage.
